name: The Schlossberg Field Maple
verified_sources: https://geodaten.graz.at/arcgis/rest/services/OGD/OGD_WFS/MapServer/8/query?where=1%3D1&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=geojson (Stadt Graz Naturdenkmale, register_id 118, object_id 112, Feldahorn/Acer campestre, owner oeffentlich)
https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkm%C3%A4ler_in_Graz (Steirisches Naturdenkmal 1270, 'Ahorn', Standort Schlossberg, KG Innere Stadt, protected 24.05.2000)
access: Free. Stands in the public Schlossberg hill park in the historic centre, open at all times; reachable on foot via paths and stairs, or by the paid Schlossbergbahn funicular.
transport: Tram 3 or 5 to the Schlossbergbahn stop, then a short walk up the hill (funicular also available, paid).
verify_notes: Two independently maintained sources agree on the exact spot: the city's own live Naturdenkmale GIS layer (fetched 2026-08-16, licence CC BY 4.0) and Wikipedia's 'Liste der Naturdenkmäler in Graz' (Steirisches ND 1270, geocoded independently, lands within 3 metres of the register point). The register gives the species as Acer campestre (Field Maple); Wikipedia's entry only says 'Ahorn' (maple, genus level) without an epithet, so the species-level identification currently rests on the register alone, not on a second independent species confirmation. Protection date given as 24.05.2000. No age, girth or height figure found in either source; the Schlossberg's mixed deciduous woodland (beech, hornbeam, ash, several maple species) is centuries-managed but that is a fact about the hill, not this specific tree, so no age is stated. Worth a reader photo with a tape measure round the trunk. The hill itself is Graz's best-known public landmark, a wooded park around the medieval fortress remains and clock tower, freely open.

access: Free. Public park (Volksgarten, 4.6 ha), open on all sides, no entry fee, no restricted hours mentioned by any source.
transport: Short walk from Graz Hauptbahnhof (about 1km) or tram/bus to Elisabethinergasse / Keplerbrücke area, then into the park via any of its entrances.

That article separately describes a roughly 80-100 year old north-south row of oaks through the park centre, but does not say this specific designated oak is part of that row, so that age is NOT applied here (avoiding the bridge-claim trap: a fact about the park's oak row is not automatically a fact about this individual protected tree). Two other Naturdenkmal trees stand in the same small park (see grz_003 and grz_004), making this a genuine walkable three-tree cluster inside one park.

name: The Augarten Field Maple

location.neighbourhood: Jakomini, at the eastern edge of the Augarten park

verified_sources: https://geodaten.graz.at/arcgis/rest/services/OGD/OGD_WFS/MapServer/8/query?where=1%3D1&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=geojson (Stadt Graz Naturdenkmale, register_id 38, object_id 75, Feldahorn/Acer campestre, owner oeffentlich)

https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkm%C3%A4ler_in_Graz (Steirisches Naturdenkmal 1009, 'Feldahorn', Standort Friedrichgasse 41, KG Jakomini, protected 05.07.1979; cites F. Hanselmayer, 'In Graz gepflanzte Laubhölzer' (1956), as already listing this tree under protection)

https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_der_Wahrnehmung (confirms Friedrichgasse 41 is a free-standing former public bath building at the eastern edge of the Grazer Augarten, a public park, with no dedicated private garden described)
access: Free to view; the address is a heritage building (now the Museum der Wahrnehmung) standing at the edge of the public Augarten park. Not confirmed on the ground whether the tree itself is inside the museum's own footprint or on the adjoining public park land, so flagged rather than stated as certain.
transport: Walkable from Graz Hauptbahnhof or the city centre (Augarten sits between the Mur river and Jakomini); tram/bus toward Elisabethstraße/Jakominiplatz, then a short walk to the Augarten.
verify_notes: Register and Wikipedia geocode within 4 metres of each other on the exact tree. Genuinely useful anecdote: Wikipedia's list cites F. Hanselmayer's 1956 survey 'In Graz gepflanzte Laubhölzer' as already recording this Feldahorn under nature protection at that date, decades before its formal 1979 designation date in this list, so the tree demonstrably existed and was already notable by 1956 (at least 70 years old as of 2026). That is the only basis for the age_min given; no growth-rate or girth-based estimate was attempted since no girth was found, and age_max is left empty because nothing bounds it above. FLAGGED for a genuine but narrow uncertainty, not about the tree's existence: the postal address belongs to a heritage bathhouse building (now Museum der Wahrnehmung) that Wikipedia describes as standing 'freely at the edge of the Augarten', with no private garden mentioned, which suggests the tree is on or immediately beside the public park rather than gated museum ground, but this was not confirmed with a source that states it explicitly. Worth a one-line access check by a future pass or reader before publishing with full confidence.

access: Free. Register lists the owner as 'oeffentlich' and the tree stands on public ground opposite the house number given (a street-side position), on the Ruckerlberg hillside in Geidorf.

verify_notes: Register and Wikipedia geocode within 2 metres. No age is derived from this girth because no specific published growth-rate figure for Quercus robur was verified during this pass; deriving a number from girth without that citation would be guessing dressed as a calculation, which the rules forbid. 'Gegenüber' (opposite) in the register means the tree stands across the street from house number 54, i.e. on the public verge/hillside, not in a private garden.

access: Free. Register lists the owner as 'oeffentlich'; stands on public ground opposite the house number given, about 40m from grz_007 along the same street.

verify_notes: Register and Wikipedia geocode within 3 metres. Field-measured trunk circumference of 4.90 m in 2015 (recorded as girth_cm), substantially thicker than its neighbour at Panoramagasse 54 (2.80 m) despite the same protection date (11.07.1979) and near-identical address, which is worth a line in the story: two oaks protected on the same day, one nearly twice the other's girth. Not a register 'twin' in the corrupted-duplicate sense: two visibly different, separately measured trees roughly 40m apart on the same street.

name: The Eggenberg Weymouth Pine

location.neighbourhood: Eggenberg (Schlosspark Eggenberg, within the palace grounds)

verified_sources: https://geodaten.graz.at/arcgis/rest/services/OGD/OGD_WFS/MapServer/8/query?where=1%3D1&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=geojson (Stadt Graz Naturdenkmale, register NUMMER 11, OBJEKT_ID 62, Weymouthskiefer/Pinus strobus, owner oeffentlich)

access: Paid entry: the tree stands inside Schlosspark Eggenberg, the grounds of Schloss Eggenberg (UNESCO World Heritage palace), run by Universalmuseum Joanneum. This pass did not independently reconfirm the current park-only ticket price or hours versus the palace/museum tour price; state plainly that entry is paid and point to the museum's own current prices page rather than quoting a figure.
transport: Graz public transport toward the Eggenberg district; Eggenberger Allee 90 is the palace's signposted main entrance. Exact tram/bus line not independently confirmed this pass.
verify_notes: Two independent official sources agree within about 3 metres: the City of Graz's own live Naturdenkmale GIS register (register NUMMER 11) and Wikipedia's separately maintained 'Liste der Naturdenkmäler in Graz' (Steirisches Naturdenkmal 986), which additionally carries a real, dated field measurement (3.70 m girth, 16 October 2016, height estimated ca. 27 m) citing monumentaltrees.com and a Flickr album as its own sources, so those two secondary corroborations exist without this pass needing to scrape monumentaltrees.com directly (its Cloudflare challenge 403s automated fetches, confirmed this pass, consistent with BRIEF_RESEARCH.md's known edge). This is the strongest INDIVIDUAL specimen in the wider Eggenberg planting: it carries its own measured girth and its own Naturdenkmal citation, unlike the three other Weymouth pines and five planes at the same address (ND 977-985, excluding 986), which share the address and protection date but have no individuating measurement or record in either source and read as one avenue/grove rather than separate collectible points (see leads file). Girth recorded as girth_cm per standing instruction; no age derived because no cited Pinus strobus growth-rate figure was in hand this pass, so age_estimate is left empty rather than guessed. Alive-now evidence is the register's current (fetched 2026-08-17) live listing plus the 2016 field measurement citation; no more recent dated photo was independently viewed this pass. Stands about 57 metres from grz_010 (the Eggenberg Copper Beech), inside the same palace park, forming a small two-tree second walk roughly 3.5km from Graz's grz_001-008 cluster.
